'''Dwaine O. Cowan''' (25 November 1935 – 5 May 2006) was an American [[chemist]]. He was a professor of chemistry at [[Johns Hopkins University]].  He is best known for his pioneering work in the field of [[organic conductor]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cowan |first1=Dwaine |title=Electron transfer in a new highly conducting donor-acceptor complex |journal=J. Am. Chem. Soc. |date=February 1973 |volume=95 |issue=3 |pages=948–949 |doi=10.1021/ja00784a066|bibcode=1973JAChS..95..948F }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Cowan |first1=Dwaine |title=Advanced Organic Solid State Materials: Volume 173 (MRS Proceedings) |date=1990 |publisher=Materials Research Society |location=New York, New York |isbn=978-1-107-41022-0}}</ref><ref>Gubser DU, Fuller WW, Poehler TO, Cowan DO, Lee M, Potember RS, Chiang LY, Bloch AN., Magnetic susceptibility and resistive transitions of superconducting (TMTSF)Cl2O4: Critical magnetic fields, Physical Review B. 1981, 24: 478-480.</ref>  His other research interests included [[organometallic chemistry]], [[organic photochemistry]],<ref>{{cite book |last1=Cowan |first1=Dwaine |title=Elements of organic photochemistry |date=1976 |publisher=Plenum Press |isbn= 0306308215 |edition=First}}</ref> [[organic chemistry]], [[metallocene]]s<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cowan |first1=Dwaine O. |last2=LeVanda |first2=Carole |last3=Park |first3=Jongsei |last4=Kaufman |first4=Frank |title=Organic solid state. VIII. Mixed-valence ferrocene chemistry |journal=Accounts of Chemical Research |date=May 2002 |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=1–7 |doi=10.1021/ar50061a001}}</ref> and the synthesis of [[heterocyclic compounds]] containing sulfur, selenium, and tellurium.<ref>Klaus Bechgaard,  Dwaine O. Cowan  and  Aaron N. Bloch, Synthesis of the organic conductor tetramethyltetraselenofulvalenium 7,7,8,8-tetracyano-p-quinodimethanide (TMTSF–TCNQ)[4,4′,5,5′-tetramethyl-Δ2,2′-bis-1,3-diselenolium 3,6-bis-(dicyanomethylene)cyclohexadienide], J. Chem. Soc., Chem. Commun., 1974,0, 937-938.</ref>

== Education ==
He received a B.S. in chemistry from [[Fresno State College]] in 1958 and a Ph.D. in chemistry from [[Harry Stone Mosher]] at [[Stanford University]] in 1962.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cowan |first1=Dwaine |title=Chemistry Tree - Dwaine O. Cowan Family Tree |url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/tree.php?pid=70905 |website=Chemistry Tree |publisher=The Academic Family Tree |accessdate=2 February 2019}}</ref>

==Research==
Cowan was a popular figure in physical organic chemistry during his thirty-year career. He is considered to be the father of "organic conductors and superconductors",<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chemeducator.org/bibs/0014003/14090118gk.htm|title=Dwaine O. Cowan (1935–2006): The Father of Organic Conductors and Superconductors |publisher=chemeducator.org}}</ref> an area of science and technology that cuts across the disciplines of chemistry, physics and materials science.

Cowan was invited to contribute a special report titled "The Organic Solid State" on the subject of organic conductors to ''[[Chemical and Engineering News]]'' (July 21, 1986).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cowan |first1=Dwaine |title=The Organic Solid State: Organic materials show interesting and useful electrical, magnetic, and optical properties in the solid state |journal=Chemical and Engineering News |date=July 21, 1986 |volume=64 |issue=29 |pages=28–45|doi=10.1021/cen-v064n029.p028 }}</ref>

Cowan and his students have authored 190 scientific articles, four patents and two monographs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/publications.php?pid=70905|title=Dwaine O. Cowan - Publications|publisher=academictree.org}}</ref> He co-authored a book with Ronald Drisko entitled ''Elements of Organic Photochemistry'' ({{ISBN|978-1-4684-2130-9}}).<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9781468421323|title = Elements of Organic Photochemistry &#124; SpringerLink}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He was preceded in death by his wife, LaVon "Bonnie" Adams Cowan; and his parents Oliver and EvaBelle Cowan.{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}

==Awards==
He received a number of major awards including [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] Fellowship (1968-1970), [[Guggenheim Fellowship]], [[University of Basel]], [[Switzerland]] (1970-1971), elected [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (1989) and the [[Alexander von Humboldt]] Senior Scientist for the [[University of Heidelberg]], [[Germany]] (1992- 1993).<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Kauffman |first=George B. |date=6 June 2009 |title=Dwaine O. Cowan (1935–2006): The Father of Organic Conductors and Superconductors |url=http://chemeducator.org/bibs/0014003/14090118gk.htm |journal=The Chemical Educator |volume=14 |issue=3}}</ref>
